title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

errors: The boxed formula ∂T = (Ṫ∩T) ⊔ (T∩∂L), and the claim that every extremity not in ∂L lies on the frontier, require L to be densely ordered (e.g. connected, like a real segment). In a discrete order such as Z, {a} is open, so [a,b] has empty frontier while ∂[a,b] = {a,b}.

The disjoint union fails for a singleton at an end of L. For L=[0,1] and T={0}: Ṫ∩T = {0} = T∩∂L. This explains the crossed-out special case 'si Card T = 1'; the boxed statement needs T not reduced to a point (or L reduced to a point), or ⊔ replaced by ∪.

∂L_{>=a} = {a} is only correct when L has no largest element (similarly for L_{<=a} and a least element). In general ∂L_{>=a} = {a} ∪ ({ex L} ∩ L), as the boxed formula itself gives. The marginal proviso seems to be patching this.
Uniqueness of the writing T' = T∖α also requires density. In Z, ]a,b] = [a+1,b].

ideas.what: Absolute boundary of an interval as its set of extremities, compared with the topological frontier in the ambient ordered line: ∂T = (Fr T ∩ T) ⊔ (T ∩ ∂L)
ideas.modern_name: boundary of a 1-dimensional manifold-with-boundary / endpoints of intervals in an order topology (manifold boundary vs. topological frontier)

ideas.what: Classification of intervals (tronçons) as closed intervals minus a subset of their endpoints, with uniqueness of this presentation
ideas.modern_name: intervals of a dense linear order; closure/endpoint description

ideas.what: Preparatory vocabulary for 'réseaux via découpages' (networks built by cutting lines into intervals), in the spirit of tame/combinatorial topology
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/tame topology of 1-dimensional complexes (cf. o-minimal cell decomposition in dimension 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries et al. for o-minimal tame topology; Grothendieck's programme in Esquisse d'un programme §5
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses 'topologie modérée' in general terms; this specific formalism is not published as far as I know

deep.surprise_reason: The page is elementary bookkeeping about endpoints versus frontiers of intervals in an ordered line. It is correct up to minor degenerate cases (density, singleton at an endpoint of L, L with extremities). It is of historical interest only as part of the unpublished 1986 'réseaux' set-up; there is no new mathematics here.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, "T'" in "T' ∩ T ⊂ ∂T ⊂ (T'∩T) ∪ ∂L" and in the boxed formula is the dotted letter Ṫ (frontier of T), not T prime.
The heading before the list of forms reads "Tronçons :" (consistent with the next page), not "Tranches".
"(a≠σ" and "(a≠α)" should read "(a ≠ or(L))" and "(a ≠ ex(L))" respectively, matching page 24's notation or(L), ex(L).
The crossed-out line reads "si Card T = 1, ∂T = Ṫ = T" (dot over T).
The marginal NB appears to say the writing is unique for T ≠ T', with T obtained as the adhérence (closure) of T'. This is tentative.
